name.text: Area Calculation Using Double Integrals for a Region Bounded by Curves

questiontext.text:
We can use double integral to calculate the area of the region inside \(r_1={@r1@}\) and outside \(r_2={@r2@}\) by following the given steps.

Below is a quick sketch of the region \(D\) that we want to find its area.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Below is a quick sketch of the region \(D\) that we want to find its area.

[[jsxgraph]] var aa = {#aa#}; var bb = {#bb#}; // bounding box dimensions change to have 2 square space above and below curves JXG.Options.text.useMathJax=true; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-(aa+bb+7)/2, aa+4, (aa+bb+7)/2, -bb-3], axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, keepaspectratio: true }); // setting display styles for objects var curveStyle = { fixed: true, highlight: false, curveType:'polar', strokeWidth:2 }; var fillStyle = { fixed: true, highlight: false, color:'lime', opacity:0.4, strokeOpacity:0 }; var pointStyle = { fixed: true, highlight: false, visible: true, showinfobox: false, fillOpacity: 0, strokeOpacity: 0, showLabel: true, useMathJax: true, parse: true, label: { fontSize: 15, highlight: false } }; var lineStyle = { fixed: true, highlight: false, strokeColor: 'black' }; // larger blue curve curveStyle.strokeColor = 'blue'; var function1 = board.create('curve', [ function(phi){return aa+2*Math.sin(phi)}, [0,0], 0, function(){return 2*Math.PI} ], curveStyle); // smaller red curve curveStyle.strokeColor = 'red'; var function2 = board.create('curve', [ function(phi){return bb-1*Math.sin(phi)}, [0,0], 0, function(){return 2*Math.PI} ], curveStyle); // shading upper difference between curves var shading = board.create('curvedifference', [function1, function2], fillStyle) // finding and labelling curve intersections pointStyle.name = "\\(\\alpha\\)" pointStyle.label.offset = [10,-10]; var intersect1 = board.create('intersection', [function1, function2, 1], pointStyle); pointStyle.name = "\\(\\beta\\)" pointStyle.label.offset = [-10,-10]; pointStyle.label.anchorX = 'right' var intersect2 = board.create('intersection', [function1, function2, 0], pointStyle); // lines from origin to intersections var line1 = board.create('segment', [[0,0], intersect1], lineStyle) var line1 = board.create('segment', [[0,0], intersect2], lineStyle) [[/jsxgraph]]

Step 1: In order to determine the limits of \(\theta\) such that \(\alpha\leq \theta\leq \beta\),

\(\qquad\) write the two equations as equivalent of themselves as shown.

\(\qquad\) \({@r1@}={@r2@}\)

\(\qquad\) \(\sin(\theta)={@expr1@}\)

\(\qquad\) \(\sin(\theta)={@expr1@} \implies \theta=\sin^{-1}({@expr1@})={@alpha@}\)

\(\qquad\) This is the first angle in the fourth quadrant, \(α={@alpha@}\)

\(\qquad\) Recall that sine in the fourth quadrant is always negative.

\(\qquad\) Therefore, the second angle will simply be \(\beta=\pi-\alpha=\pi+{@-1*alpha@}={@beta@}\)

Step 2: The limits obtained are,

\(\qquad\) \( {@alpha@} \leq \theta \leq {@beta@}\),

\(\qquad\) \({@r2@}\leq r \leq {@r1@}\)

Step 3: In order to integrate the function with respect to r with polar coordinates,

\(\qquad \quad\) In this case we need to recall that \(dA=r dr dθ\).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle A &= \int \int_D dA \\ &= \int_{{@alpha@}}^{{@beta@}} \int_{{@r2@}}^{@r1@} rdrd\theta \\ &= \int_{{@alpha@}}^{{@beta@}} {@r_int@}\left.\begin{matrix} & \\ & \end{matrix}\right|_{{@r2@}}^{@r1@} d\theta \\ &= \int_{{@alpha@}}^{{@beta@}} \left({@r_int_limits@}\right) d\theta \end{align} \)

Step 4: We compute the \(\theta\) integration.

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle A &= \int_{{@alpha@}}^{{@beta@}} \left({@r_int_limits@}\right) d\theta \\ &={@theta_int@}\left.\begin{matrix} & \\ & \end{matrix}\right|_{{@alpha@}}^{{@beta@}} \\ &={@expr3@} - {@expr4@} \\ &= {@ta4@} \end{align} \)

Remember \(\alpha\) is the angle in the \(4^th\) quadrant. To compute \(\beta\) simply take \(pi-\alpha\) which is the angle in the third quadrant of the circle.
